strong_findings.citation: A. Riotto, I. Tkachev, "What if dark matter is bosonic and self-interacting?", Phys. Lett. B 484, 177 (2000), doi:10.1016/S0370-2693(00)00660-2, arXiv:astro-ph/0003388
strong_findings.summary: Self-interacting bosonic dark matter is put forward as a cure for cuspy cores and too many dwarf galaxies. In a virialized clump the phase-space density exceeds unity, so scattering is Bose-enhanced and the clump Bose-condenses. For v_e = 100 km/s, which the authors say approximately corresponds to dwarf-galaxy cores, the relaxation time is shorter than the age of the Universe above a stated coupling, and 'the Bose condensate in the center of gravitational well should form'. The paper then derives the core density that the condensate's self-annihilation allows. This is the notebook's 'below a critical velocity dispersion the core of a halo condenses' (#1 §5.2), in 2000.
strong_findings.difference: It states the same form of C6 as Sikivie and Yang 2009 and Berezhiani and Khoury 2015, and states it earlier. The condensation comes from contact self-interaction and Bose statistics, not from an attraction gated in relative velocity. The result is one condensate in the core, not several velocity streams, and it needs degenerate bosons (the record's classicality theorem). The paper speaks of a condensate in the centre of the well, never of momentum space: reading it as momentum-space clumping is the notebook's identification, the same reading that makes Sikivie-Yang and Berezhiani-Khoury partial. Its relaxation rate (Bose-enhanced scattering in a virialized clump, after Tkachev 1991 and Semikoz-Tkachev 1995) is the kind of rate the record's wave island uses (#11 §9 (ii), 'Bose-enhanced, LPT-style'), without the gate. Its ref. [14], Tkachev, Phys. Lett. B 261, 289 (1991), was not retrieved (†).

strong_findings.citation: L. Berezhiani, J. Khoury, "Theory of dark matter superfluidity", Phys. Rev. D 92, 103510 (2015), arXiv:1507.01019
strong_findings.summary: Dark matter made of eV-mass axion-like particles with strong self-interactions condenses into a superfluid core inside galaxies, where the velocity dispersion (and so the temperature) is low; in clusters, where the dispersion is higher, it is partly or wholly in the normal phase. In the condensed phase the dark matter behaves as collective excitations rather than individual collisionless particles. This is the notebook's form of C6, 'below a critical velocity dispersion the core of a halo condenses', with 'superfluid-like cores in dwarfs' (#1 §5.2), and the same split between galaxies and clusters as the program's knee.
strong_findings.difference: The condensate is a Bose–Einstein superfluid produced by strong contact self-interactions and Bose degeneracy, not by an attraction gated in relative velocity; there is one condensate, not several velocity streams; the aim is MOND phenomenology through phonons coupled to baryons; nothing is conjugate or momentum-polarized. Citation graph: forward citations filtered for 'momentum space' or 'velocity space' with 'condens' gave one unrelated thesis; the references are the BEC-halo lineage (Sin, Ji–Sin, Böhmer–Harko, Sikivie–Yang, Guth–Hertzberg–Prescod-Weinstein).

quotes.text: The condensate has a polytropic equation of state P~rho^3 giving rise to a superfluid core within galaxies.
due to the higher velocity dispersion in clusters, and correspondingly higher temperature, the DM in clusters is either in a mixture of superfluid and normal phase, or fully in the normal phase
Instead of behaving as individual collisionless particles, the DM superfluid is more aptly described as collective excitations.

verified: Confirmed, for the notebook's condensed-core sub-claim: superfluid (Bose-condensed) cores in galaxies, and a normal or mixed phase in clusters 'due to the higher velocity dispersion', which matches #1 §5.2's 'below a critical velocity dispersion the core of a halo condenses' and 'superfluid-like cores'. strong_findings.citation: P. Sikivie, Q. Yang, "Bose-Einstein Condensation of Dark Matter Axions", Phys. Rev. Lett. 103, 111301 (2009), arXiv:0901.1106
strong_findings.summary: Argues that cold dark-matter axions are driven by their own gravitational interaction to thermalize and Bose-condense: (almost) all axions go into one quantum state, with condensate patches about the size of the horizon, so the axions collect in one state while staying spread through space. In a homogeneous universe that state is the lowest momentum mode, which is condensation in momentum space in Einstein's sense. Continued rethermalization puts infalling axions into the lowest-energy state at fixed angular momentum (net rotation), which the authors use to explain caustic rings; the full treatment is Erken, Sikivie, Tam and Yang, Phys. Rev. D 85, 063520 (2012), arXiv:1111.1157. It is the closest published statement that dark matter collects collectively in momentum space through its own attraction.
strong_findings.difference: Ordinary gravity plus Bose degeneracy drives the condensation; there is no attraction gated in relative velocity, no conjugate (p-polarized) sector and no Born reciprocity. The outcome is one condensate in the lowest-energy state, not a smooth Maxwellian fragmenting into a few discrete streams at different mean velocities. It holds only for highly degenerate bosons, the same requirement the record's classicality theorem reaches (#11 §9 (i)). The paper does not use the words 'momentum space'; equating Bose condensation with momentum-space clumping is the textbook reading and the notebook's own ('below a critical velocity dispersion the core of a halo condenses — momentum-space clumping, realized', #1 §5.2). Its long-range coherence is disputed by Guth, Hertzberg and Prescod-Weinstein 2015 (evidence-against below). Citation graph: the 562 citing papers filtered for 'momentum space', 'velocity space', 'discrete flows' and 'condensation in momentum space' contain no statement of velocity-space fragmentation; the 35 references are the axion and BEC-halo lineage (Sin 1992/94, Böhmer–Harko 2007, Semikoz–Tkachev 1995).

quotes.text: We show that cold dark matter axions thermalize and form a Bose-Einstein condensate.
Axion BEC means that (almost) all axions go to one state.
Thus gravitational interactions cause the axions to thermalize and form a BEC
We expect overlapping condensate patches with typical size of order the horizon.

verified: Confirmed, for one form of C6 only. strong_findings.citation: A. H. Guth, M. P. Hertzberg, C. Prescod-Weinstein, "Do Dark Matter Axions Form a Condensate with Long-Range Correlation?", Phys. Rev. D 92, 103513 (2015), arXiv:1412.5930
strong_findings.summary: Examines the Sikivie–Yang claim and argues that thermalization through attractive interactions (gravity, attractive self-coupling) produces localized Bose clumps (stars, solitons) with only short-range correlation; only repulsive interactions drive long-range order. A condensate forms, but it is not coherent over cosmological distances.
strong_findings.difference: Weighs against the gravity-driven route to a condensate that is localized in momentum and spread through space, the published form closest to C6. It concerns attraction in position; it does not treat an attraction gated in velocity, whose Born-dual reading would localize in momentum rather than position, so it is not a test of the record's gated model.

quotes.text: there is an essential difference between the thermalization and formation of a condensate due to repulsive interactions, which can indeed drive long-range order, and that due to attractive interactions, which can lead to localized Bose clumps (stars or solitons) that only exhibit short range correlation
we conclude that while a Bose-Einstein condensate is formed, the claim of long-range correlation is unjustified

verified: Confirmed, within its scope. It argues that condensation driven by attractive interactions gives localized clumps with short-range correlation, against the gravity-driven, spatially coherent condensate of Sikivie and Yang, the published form closest to C6. not_found_statements.statement: No paper found that states that dark matter (or any matter) clumps collectively in momentum space by the Jeans mechanism with position and velocity exchanged: that an attraction acting between particles of similar velocity makes a smooth Maxwellian fragment into a few discrete velocity streams spread through space; nor any paper proposing that dark matter is matter of the conjugate (momentum) polarization that clumps in momentum space as ordinary matter clumps in position space. Momentum-space condensation of dark matter appears in print only as Bose–Einstein condensation or superfluidity (one state, degenerate bosons: Sikivie–Yang, Berezhiani–Khoury, Levkov et al.); discrete velocity flows only from cold infall or accretion (Sikivie et al., Zemp et al.); velocity concentration by an interaction only in flocking models (Ha–Tadmor); and a Born-reciprocal momentum-space attraction only without a clumping claim (Delbourgo–Lashmar, Burgers–Mantz–Prokopec).

No source found, in any venue searched, in which dark matter clumps or condenses in velocity or momentum space through a collective instability, a Jeans analysis is run with position and velocity exchanged, or dark matter flocks by velocity. OpenAlex title/abstract phrase searches for 'clumping in velocity space', 'velocity space clumping', 'clumps in velocity space', 'condensation in velocity space' and 'Jeans instability' + 'momentum space' returned 0. Full-text hits are stellar moving groups, cluster substructure and cold-dark-matter fine-grained streams. 'Murmuration' hits are unrelated (elliptic-curve murmurations). DataCite and Zenodo hits are non-reviewed unified theories. The closest material remains what the known list holds (Sikivie-Yang, Berezhiani-Khoury, Zemp et al., Vogelsberger-White, Ghosh's Born-Kothari condensation).

No lineage paper proposes that matter clumps in momentum or velocity space through its own collective attraction. The lineages treat momentum space as curved geometry (Born, Kadyshevsky, Moffat, Wheeler), a velocity fibre (Finsler, tangent-bundle, Caianiello), or a source of velocity-dependent gravity (kinetic gas), never as a space in which matter gathers into clumps.

Holds for the founding image itself, with two qualifications. (1) Its condensed-core form was published before the searcher's earliest partial: Riotto and Tkachev 2000 have Bose condensation in dwarf-galaxy cores. Bosonic dark-matter halos go back further: Sin, Phys. Rev. D 50, 3650 (1994), on the halo as a Bose liquid (abstract read), and Tkachev 1986 and 1991 (†, not read). Every published form is one Bose condensate, not a few velocity streams from a gated attraction. (2) The clause 'velocity concentration by an interaction only in flocking models' is incomplete. Fragmentation of a uniform distribution into several discrete, equally spaced clusters by an interaction gated in the difference of the variable is established in compromise (bounded-confidence) dynamics (Ben-Naim, Krapivsky and Redner 2003), a dissipative, non-Hamiltonian setting; for velocities it amounts to inelastic collisions below a threshold. My own searches (velocity- and momentum-space instability, instability in or unstable in momentum space, gravitational instability with momentum space and reciprocity, dual matter and dual sector with momentum or velocity space, Born reciprocity with clustering or instability, a web search for a velocity-space phase transition of halos, Crossref on velocity-space Jeans instability) found no statement of the Jeans problem with x and v exchanged, nor of conjugate or dual matter clumping in momentum space. The dual-sector dark-matter papers named by the searcher (Freidel-Kowalski-Glikman-Leigh-Minic 2021, Minic 2020, Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2022, Hübsch-Minic 2026) contain no clumping, clustering or localization in a dual or momentum space (grep of full texts).
